violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: working containers of salt, sugar, pepper, cooking oil, spices, herbs; squeeze bottles of oil, tamarind sauce, mint sauce stored on cook line and throughout establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC labeled all aforementioned working containers and squeeze bottles.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed plastic containers/cups used to dispense from bulk containers of salt, flour, rice, lentils and etc.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS instructed management to remove the plastic cups and provide food scoops that have handles. The handles shall set up out of the food. PIC removed plastic cups from bulk containers of salt, flour, rice, lentils and etc.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Observed manufacturer garlic single use containers being re-used to store dry spices.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. PIC agreed to stop re-use of manufacturer single-use containers and moved dry spices into reusable containers.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: Observed raw chicken stored above cooked goat.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC placed raw chicken below cooked goat.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: Observed raw chicken sitting in the bath of water in prep sink.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EHS discussed proper thawing methods with PIC. PIC completely submerged raw chicken under running water at the water temperature of 70F.

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: EHS OBSERVED UNCOVERED DRY SPICES BEING STORED NEXT TO HAND SINK AND UNDER PAPER TOWELS WHERE IT CAN BE CONTAMINATED BY WATER FROM HANDS.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. PIC COVERED SPICES SO THEY COULDN’T BE CONTAMINATED BY HANDWASHING AND DRYING.
